articles.title: Posting twist sees Panaji, Porvorim SDPOs swap charges
articles.summary: Goa Police SP HQ order swaps additional charge between Panaji and Porvorim SDPOs, drawing criticism over procedure and authority for DySP postings.
articles.body: Panaji: In an unusual order issued by SP (headquarters) Tushar Vernekar, the officers already serving as sub-divisional police officers in Porvorim and Panaji have been given additional charge of each other’s posts. This means both Panaji and Porvorim will have two officers overseeing investigations.Senior police officers said the order was not issued as per procedure. They said postings of SP are issued by govt, while postings of DySP are handled by the police establishment board.The order, issued on Sept 28, 2026, said: “Vishwesh Karpe, SP presently holding the charge of SDPO Panaji shall hold the charge of SDPO Porvorim, with immediate effect, until further orders. Similarly, Sudesh Naik, SDPO Porvorim shall hold the charge of SDPO Panaji, with immediate effect, until further orders. This is issued with the approval of DGP, Goa.”The order does not say the officers are giving up their existing duties. Despite this, both officers took charge of the new offices.Earlier, on Sept 10, 2026, the state govt had transferred SP Vishwesh Karpe as SDPO Porvorim and given him charge of SDPO Panaji. That order said Karpe would hold charge of SDPO Panaji and give up charge of SDPO Porvorim with immediate effect.Former deputy inspector general of police Bosco George criticised the Sept 28 order. He said postings of DySP made by the police establishment board, while postings of SP are issued by govt. He also said approval from DGP was not required.He said the order reminded him of a James Bond quote, “Once is a mistake, second is a coincidence, third is enemy action.”“In this case, the first mistake is mass promotion to SPs; second mistake is SPs being posted as SDPOs, degrading the post; third, posting is usurped in the name of DG, as DSP’s posting is done by police establishment board (PEB) and SP’s posting is issued by the govt; there is no requirement of DG approval. This is indeed an enemy action,” George said.In Jan 2026, state govt promoted 19 DySP to the post of SP. Nearly a year later, some of them are still being posted in DySP roles. articles.title: ‘Clarify why no decision taken’: HC to Punjab over delay in appointing regular DGP
articles.summary: Punjab & Haryana HC asks Punjab to explain delay in appointing regular DGP, seeks chief secretary affidavit; UPSC panel sent in July 2026, next hearing Oct 13.
articles.body: Chandigarh: The Punjab and Haryana high court on Thursday directed Punjab govt to take an appropriate decision on the appointment of a regular director general of police (DGP), observing that an ad hoc arrangement for the top police post “ought not be allowed for an indefinite period”.A division bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor also directed the state to place before the court an affidavit of the chief secretary, informing it about the decision taken on the appointment. The next hearing is on Oct 13.The bench was hearing a public interest litigation filed by advocate Nikhil Thamman, who appeared in person, alleging that Punjab had failed to appoint a regular DGP despite directions issued by the Supreme Court regarding the selection and minimum tenure of the police chief.The state govt informed the high court that an affidavit had been filed by Punjab under secretary, stating that the issue was also being monitored by the Supreme Court in Prakash Singh and others versus Union of India, pending as Writ Petition (Civil) No. 310 of 1996. The affidavit was taken on record.The HC was also informed that Punjab had filed a compliance affidavit before the Supreme Court, stating that it had, on April 6 forwarded the complete proposal to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) for convening the empanelment committee meeting for preparing a panel for the appointment.According to the affidavit, the UPSC empanelment committee subsequently met and, after assessment, recommended a panel of three officers for the post. The affidavit stated that the panel was under the “active consideration” of Punjab govt and that the state was taking steps for the appointment.Thamman told the bench that the UPSC had recommended the panel of three officers in the first week of July 2026. The state counsel, additional advocate general Chanchal K Singhla, submitted the matter was under active consideration.The bench then observed: “In the event a panel has already been forwarded by the Union Public Service Commission in the first week of July 2026, we would like the state of Punjab to clarify as to why no decision is taken in the matter, when the panel is already received way back in July 2026.”The HC observed that the appointment “is of importance for maintenance of the law and order”. “An ad hoc arrangement for such purposes ought not be allowed for an indefinite period,” it observed.The petitioner stated that the post of DGP has continued to be held through an additional-charge arrangement since July 2022. Tetition refers to an order dated July 4, 2022, under which IPS officer Gaurav Yadav was given additional charge of DGP during the leave period of the then incumbent DGP, V K Bhawra.
